transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-30
Time: 14:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Marco Diaz (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Derek Wu (Velox CTO), Sandra Lopez (Lead ML Eng), Tom Rivera (Infra), Maya Chen (Product)

Summary:
Quick weekly POC sync focused on TTFT (time-to-first-token) regressions under microburst traffic, streaming handshake improvements, and kernel selection strategy for Velox Retail's inference profile. Agreed on targeted microbenchmark and canary routing plan; need prod seqlen distribution and follow-up run.

Topics:
- TTFT variability and microbursts
- Streaming path handshake and buffer sizing
- Sequence length distribution and kernel tradeoffs
- Canary/fallback routing and smaller-model hedging
- Next experiments and deliverables

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Marco (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, looks like we have Derek, Sandra, Tom, Maya, and Priya from our side. Does that match?
[00:12] Derek (Velox): Yep that matches. Morning from me, afternoon for you all.
[00:18] Priya (Redwood SE): Morning! I pushed the new bench harness to the pilot repo, branch "microburst-aug26" — there's a README but I'll link it after.
[00:27] Sandra (Velox): Saw that, thanks. We tried a naive run yesterday and saw TTFT spikes around 180–220 ms on a 70th percentile which is... higher than we'd like.
[00:36] Marco: Ok, good context. Today's goal is: understand the shape of those spikes, whether they come from kernel selection at certain seqlens or from streaming handshake microbursts, and land on a concrete test to run before next week.
[00:50] Derek: We also want to understand cost impact if we do hedging to smaller variant for those spikes — we have a pretty tight cost threshold.
[00:58] Priya: Right. One note up front: some of the early logs use the term "kv cache stall" in the harness because of how we log cache misses; that might be noisy. We'll try to normalize naming.
[01:10] Tom (Infra): Quick infra note — our traffic is bursty around search index updates, which is when we see the microbursts; not a steady tail. We can provision for an experiment window next Wed if needed.
[01:20] Marco: Great, thanks. Priya, can you walk through the bench results you ran and the hypothesis?
[01:26] Priya: Sure. So we ran 3 slices: single-shot generation (no streaming), streaming with default buffer (t=4ms), and streaming with aggressive t=1ms buffer. The interesting bit is that TTFT improved for many cases with t=1 but we saw an odd tail around seqlen 512 where some kernels switch to a slower attention path — we suspect the runtime chose a fallback kernel because of sequence-length alignment.
[01:50] Sandra: When you say "switch to slower attention path" — is that flash-attn vs. fused-attn? Our team wasn't sure what kernel names to look for in logs.
[01:58] Priya: Exactly, our logs use internal names: "fast_attn_v2" for the optimized fused path, and "legacy_attn" for the fallback. Legacy path shows a step-up in per-token times.
[02:08] Derek: Can you quantify how much slower?
[02:11] Priya: On average per-token latency jumps 30–45% when falling back, but the real problem is the variance; during microbursts the scheduler can cause a handful of requests to hit the fallback which pushes TTFT out.
[02:24] Marco: So two levers: nudge kernel selection via seqlen padding/packing and adjust streaming handshake/buffer sizing to avoid head-of-line stalls. Also consider hedging to smaller variant for the early token to keep TTFT bounded.
[02:38] Maya: From product POV, we prefer hedging only as a safety valve — primary goal is consistent TTFT under bursts without increasing cost too much.
[02:47] Tom: On infra side, we can create a transient buffer layer to smooth bursts but that adds network hops, maybe more latency.
[02:54] Priya: Right, any extra hop could add ~10ms, so it's a tradeoff. Our plan: first try to change how the runtime picks kernels by aligning tokenization and packing to avoid the seqlen pattern that flips to legacy_attn. If that fails, use canary hedging.
[03:08] Sandra: How do we align tokenization? We have diverse prompt families — some are short queries, some are long descriptions. We'll share distribution.
[03:16] Priya: Yes please share the seqlen CSV. Also, we can experiment with quantization profile adjustments — in some runs 4-bit quant produced slightly different kernel heuristics.
[03:26] Derek: Wait, 4-bit changed kernel choice? We thought quant only impacted compute.
[03:30] Priya: It can, because some kernels are quant-friendly and the runtime may prefer a path that supports the quant layout. It's subtle but visible in the logs we collected.
[03:40] Marco: Ok. Let's talk about the microburst test you proposed.
[03:44] Priya: It's a targeted 1k-sample run that simulates short bursts (10–20 requests at high qps) with varying seqlen mixes. We'll capture per-request TTFT, per-token times, kernel selection metric, and queue depth. The goal is to see if t=1 streaming buffer plus seqlen packing mitigates the spikes.
[04:02] Sandra: Sounds good. We can provide product prompts and request templates. Note: some prompts contain PII — we'll annotate those and we only want logs with redacted content.
[04:12] Priya: Understood — we'll redact and keep only timing metadata if needed.
[04:16] Tom: For the microburst run we'll need a reserved GPU slot for an hour on Wed. I'll get that ready and share access.
[04:23] Marco: Perfect. On hedging/canary routing: I'll open a ticket to create a canary that routes 2% of streaming requests with early-token hedging to a smaller variant (redwood-mini-0.7b) and measure delta. If cost delta is acceptable, we can increase.
[04:38] Derek: If hedging adds say 8–12% cost but cuts severe TTFT spikes by 60%, that could be acceptable — but need exact numbers.
[04:46] Priya: We'll produce a small cost model tied to per-token counts for the canary. Also we'll instrument per-route cost counters in the pilot console so you can see it in near real-time.
[04:56] Maya: Any security/compliance concerns with routing to a smaller model? Our data classification is the same but just checking the policy surface.
[05:02] Marco: No different; same VPC and KMS keys apply. We will document audit logs and SSO access.
[05:07] Sandra: Ok good. A few quick quicks — (1) can you add clarity in the logs about kernel names (human-friendly), (2) include a flag to turn on verbose scheduler traces, (3) show the code path that wrote "kv cache stall" so we don't misinterpret?
[05:20] Priya: Yes to all three. I'll add a mapping table in the pilot repo and enable an opt-in verbose trace toggle.
[05:27] Marco: Great. Anything else from Velox?
[05:30] Derek: One ask — could Redwood run an end-to-end streaming handshake with header compression off? We suspect some edge proxies change packet timing.
[05:38] Priya: We can toggle that. We'll include that as a matrix dimension.
[05:41] Tom: We'll also run a network capture during the microburst window.
[05:44] Marco: Ok timeline recap: Priya runs the benchmark and posts logs by Sep 3. Sandra shares seqlen CSV by Sep 4. Marco opens canary ticket by Sep 2. Follow-up sync Sep 8.
[05:55] Derek: Good notes. Thanks all.
[05:58] Marco: Thanks everyone. We'll send minutes and links to the pilot artifacts.
[06:02] Maya: Thanks. Bye.

End of transcript.
